Comments: On site for a follow-up inspection to check for the sustained presence of gas at any of the twelve wells annuli that were cemented to surface. Selman confirmed gas show. If gas was detected then a sample was collected. 9H (115-22252) (20x13) There was 0 flow and 0 gas, there was no sample collected. (13x9) There was 0 flow and 0 gas, there was no sample collected. Selmans meter got a reading of 7.4% LEL and 3400ppm then depleted, not enough to collect a sample.

properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: REPSOL OIL & GAS USA LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 2/08/2023
Violation Code: 78A57(A)___ - CONTROL, STORAGE AND DISPOSAL OF PRODUCTION FLUIDS - Operator discharged brine and other fluids on or into the ground or into the waters of this Commonwealth.
Violation ID: 984959
Permit API: 015-20372
Unconventional: Yes
County: Bradford
Municipality: Troy Twp
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 2/10/2023
Comments: Incident Inspection of Repsol's "Lutz 015" Marcellus well site.Mike Mcnett (Repsol) called the DEP on Wednesday February 8, 2023 to report an estimated 10 gallon release of produced liquid from the dumpline onto the pad surface. I spoke with McNett on site. Two days ago Well Services was trying to unload one of the Marcellus wells at this site. When they sent produced liquid from the GPU, a union on the dumpline broke. They immediately stopped the flow, but an estimated 10 gallons leaked onto the pad surface. Immediately after the release, workers removed four 5 gallon buckets full of mostly gravel pad material under the pipe that leaked. Today they are inspecting all the unions on the dumpline. A crew is removing the insulation from the pipe during this inspection. I got electrical conductivity (EC) readings 0.80-1.4 mS/cm from moist soil below the leak. McNett filled a 55 gallon drum with additional impacted pad material during this inspection. EC readings in the pad material after that were 0.21-0.44 mS/cm. Pad material outside of the spill area has EC of 0.10-0.33.Violations cited to the 015-20372 permit are considered immediately corrected.Vegetation and rock stabilize soil of the site to comply with 102.22 Permanent Stabilization. I did not see accelerated erosion or sedimentation.Containment structures are intact. I did not observe any leaks or other deficiencies.Post Construction Stormwater Management (PCSM) controls are in place and appear to be functioning as designed. Pooled water on the pad surface in 3 separate puddles has electrical conductivity of 0.08-0.57 mS/cm with an Oakton PCST 5. Air temp 42FJLP

properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: BKV OPR LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 5/10/2013
Violation Code: 78a86 - CASING AND CEMENTING - DEFECTIVE CASING OR CEMENTING - Operator failed to report defect in a well that has defective, insufficient or improperly cemented casing to the Department within 24 hours of discovery. Operator failed to correct defect or failed to submit a plan to correct the defect for approval by the Department within 30 days.
Violation ID: 902262
Permit API: 131-20193
Unconventional: Yes
County: Wyoming
Municipality: Washington Twp
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 12/11/2020
Comments: At time of inspection, partly sunny, 54 degs. A total of (7) wells have been drilled on this pad. All (7) wells were producing at time of inspection, they are the Yarasavage 1H, 2H, 4H, 5H, 6H,7H and the Yarasavage/Solanick 3H. All the wells had (2) annular vents present and plumbed to surface. The 2" pipes are venting the (9x5) annuli, the 1" pipes are venting the (13x9) annuli. Both annular vents on all wells were open and venting. The (9x5) vents were plumbed via 2" pipe to production tanks. The (13x9) annuli are venting to atmosphere via 1" pipe. The Yarasavage 7H has an additional 2" pipe venting the capped (13x9) annulus to atmosphere. A gas check was performed at the (13x9) vent openings using a ALTAIR 5X gas meter (cal. 12/11/20). No gas was detected at any of the (13x9) vent openings. Gas meter was left on to check for gas in cellars and during walk around pad. No gas was detected in ambient air. Individual well status and pressures read from control panel at GPU's are listed below. - Yarasavage 6H - Producing, Prod. tree press. : 326.1 psi., Prod. csg. press. : 458.7 psi. - Yarasavage 7H - Producing, Prod. tree press. : 346.3 psi., Prod. csg. press. : 435.7 psi. - Yarasavage 5H - Producing, Prod. tree press. : 326.4 psi., Prod. csg. press. : 447.6 psi. - Yarasavage 4H - Producing, Prod. tree press. : 327.4 psi., Prod. csg. press. : 440.5 psi. - Yarasavage 2H - Producing, Prod. tree press. : 344.2 psi., Prod. csg. press. : 467.2 psi. - Yarasavage 1H - Producing, Prod. tree press. : 317.5 psi., Prod. csg. press. : 436.1 psi. - Yarasavage/Solanick 3H - Producing, Prod. tree press. : 325.8 psi., Prod. csg. press. : 431.3 psi. - Prod. Trees and Csgs. are being monitored w/ Cygnet system. - There is a self contained auxiliary compressor on site and running at time of inspection. - There is self contained ancillary equipment on the pad. - Took a walk around pad, no obvious concerns or violations noted

properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: RICE DRILLING B LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 7/18/2023
Violation Code: 78a66(b)1i - REPORTING AND REMEDIATING SPILLS AND RELEASES – Reporting releases – Operator or other responsible party failed to report a spill or release of a regulated substance causing or threatening pollution of the waters of this Commonwealth, in the manner required by 25 Pa. Code § 91.33 (relating to incidents causing or threatening pollution).
Violation ID: 8153119
Permit API: 125-27720
Unconventional: Yes
County: Washington
Municipality: North Bethlehem Township
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 7/18/2023
Comments: On 07/18/2023, an incident inspection was conducted at the Ironman Well Site in response to an incident report received by the Department and submitted by EQT on 07/17/2023 (CTS: 373620). I was accompanied by Matt Dracup, PGM (PADEP), Doug Oberdorf, and Jason Nicholson (EQT). Additional EQT and SPSI representatives on site. Stressed vegetation observed on north-northwest facing slope (fill side) of the Ironman pad on 07/14/2023 by an EQT contractor doing a routine site inspection. EQT representative investigated stressed vegetation on 07/17/2023 and identified it as a brine release and notified the Department. It was further investigated by EQT on 07/17/2023 w/ interim remediation activities starting on 07/18/2023. According to EQT, an approx. 5 ft x 2 ft pool of fluid was observed within area of stressed vegetation and fluid was observed sprinkling out. The overall area of stressed vegetation was approximately 25 ft x 25 ft. The release was estimated over a barrel and Act 2 remediation is anticipated. The source of the leak was identified as a small pinhole in cushion elbow at the northern most corner of the pad from the buried common dump line transferring brine flowback from the GPUs to the ASTs; approx. 70 ft northeast, away from the stressed vegetation area. Operator discovery and pre-remediation conductivity levels and incident writeup requested.Inspection observations: Area of stressed vegetation and pooled production fluid observed on fill slope below northwestern edge of pad and below compressor building on the pad. Among pooled fluid, an oily sheen was also observed. The impacted area appeared to be approx. 25 ft. x 25 ft. The area was covered with a plastic tarp upon arriving on site (Photos 1-7). SPSI crew preparing and beginning excavation to locate source of leak and begin remediation measures. Potholes to be dug on pad around approximate area of leak source to gain extent of fluid. Elevated conductivity observed within impacted area yielded readings of 14.62 mS, 9.96 mS. Readings beyond edge of impacted area, on the more northern edge of the area, displayed a reading of 1.87 mS. Additional readings within vegetation beyond edge of affected area were taken and yielded levels of 1.03 and within the area beyond the fence approximately 5 ft. at the bottom of the slope, 1.98 mS was observed within vegetation. Readings taken within the Unnamed Tributary to Daniels Run, below impacted area approximately 125 ft. north of the impacted area. Readings obtained within water and sediment of the stream w/ levels at 0.43-0.86 mS. Readings obtained within retentive berm along southeastern edge of site below pad; readings taken in water and within sediment yielded 0.33 mS and 0.60 mS (8-16). Readings taken at southern corner of the vegetated swales outlet structure, both in and around; readings of 0.46 mS within water and 0.59 mS within mud around the structure observed (17). Comments: The Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) conducted a FUI inspection at the Tilden Marcellus LLC - Pierson 801 located in Gaines Twp, Tioga Co. on 10/2/2019 @0845 hours. The weather was sunny 74 degrees. Onsite for the inspection was myself, Korey Starkey, DEP WQS; Jennifer Compton and Nathan Smelser, Tilden Marcellus; Farmer Boy Restoration; Civil and Environmental Consultants, Inc.(CEC) As of today's inspection, a large stain was observed on the gravel surface adjacent to the failed dump line measuring ~8'x4'(See Photo#1). Tilden's earthmoving sub-contractor, Farmer Boy Restoration, had used a small excavator to scrape the surface of the impacted pad area, fill slope (see photo #2) and dig a sump in the fill slope approximately 4' wide and 5' deep. Fluid that had accumulated in the bottom of the sump had a field measured conductivity of "Over Range" or >19.99mS/cm(See Photo#3). Sample 4427-192 was collected from the fluid in the fill slope sump and submitted to the DEP laboratory in Harrisburg for SAC 942 analysis. CEC consultants had delineated the extent of the impacted area with white flags. The excavator, and CEC, were currently working to remove soil with an elevated conductivity in an area below the toe of the fill slope(See Photo#4,5). The excavated sump was then expanded across the fill slope. A wet gravel layer was observed ~3' below the pad surface that appeared to be the source of the >19.99mS/cm fluid entering the sump(See Photo#6). Jennifer Compton and CEC continued to screen the fill slope area and remove additional material. The impacted material was being staged on the pad surface, on the interior of the gas line, awaiting the delivery of more disposal boxes. Ms. Compton was also awaiting the delivery of a super sucker truck to remove additional pad material. Tilden Marcellus and CEC were advised to contact the DEP Environment Cleanups and Brownfields (ECB) Program to facilitate cleanup activities going forward. Violations cited previously in inspection report#2939891, dated 9/30/2019 are cited as OUTSTANDING against the 2H well, API#117-20309 at this time. We departed the site @1200 hours.

Inspection Date: 1/21/2026
Comments: On 1/21/2026, DEP representative John Rogers conducted a drilling/completions inspection at the Seneca Resource's Taft 851 well site located in Middlebury Township, Tioga County. It was 18 degrees and overcast when I arrived on location. The original south pad and access road for the Taft 851 1V well have been returned to original grade and vegetated.When I arrived at the active north pad, I met with Seneca's Mark McCormick who described current operations as follows. Drilling to total depth has been completed on eight new gas wells at the site. Crews were on site, prepping for upcoming stimulation operations on the eight wells. Toe preps were conducted last week to open the sleeves of each well. Frac equipment was being mobilized to the location. In addition to 28 frac tanks that were stationed on the west side of the pad during previous operations, four pump down frac tanks, two gas buster frac tanks and five working frac tanks have been staged on the pad. Mark expects stimulation activities to start the first or second week of February, depending when the crew completes stimulation activities at a different pad. Mark expects stimulation activities on the eight wells to be completed by the end of June 2026.Five wells have been completed at the site and were staged for production. Three sand separators remain near the wells but have been disconnected. I did witness a secondary containment measuring 6' x 6' with a valve connecting two pipes in it that had liquid in the containment that field tested at 19.99 mS conductance. The pipe connects the east production tank to one of the frac tanks on the west side of the pad. There was visible evidence of a release of material that overtopped the secondary containment structure. The release was observed in a frozen state, on the unprotected ground in an area measuring approximately 18" x 36" x 0.5" deep. I reported this to Mark who will contact production to have it cleaned.Three sediment traps and one sediment basin have been installed on site and along the access road. They have not been converted to PCSM BMPs yet. Sediment trap 3 and the sediment basin did have standing water/ice. Temporary compost filter socks remain installed throughout the site. Violations are still outstanding for inspection ID 3846665 and ID 3855651 for puddles of water with elevated conductance discovered on the pad surface and in the sediment basin during completion operations.The DEP recommends that Seneca continues to monitor the conditions on the pad surface and the sediment basin and remove elevated conductance fluids and soils as discovered. Prevent elevated conductance fluids from leaving the facility and causing pollution to the waters of the Commonwealth. I left the site at 1300 hours.

The well tag did not appear to match the correct operator information, however the API number appeared to be correct. I observed a significant amount of fluid emanating from the well. The Department requests clarification as to what caused the release, the quantity of fluid released and how this was determined, how long it is believed the release was occurring. Violation Code: 78.88(d) - OPERATING WELLS - MECHANICAL INTEGRITY OF OPERATING WELLS - Operator failed to immediately notify the Department and take corrective actions to repair or replace defective equipment or casing for wells exhibiting progressive corrosion, rusting or other signs of equipment deterioration that compromise the integrity of the well.
Violation ID: 972186
Permit API: 063-31807
Unconventional: No
County: Indiana
Municipality: Grant Twp
Inspection Type: Administrative/File Review
Inspection Date: 10/17/2022
Comments: EPA Mechanical Integrity Test was conducted on 10/12/2022 at 09:58. Tubing pressure at commencement of test was 2225 p.s.i. Tubing annulus was filled with freshwater and pressured up to 800 p.s.i. MIT concluded at 10:28. Final pressure on tubing annuls was 800 p.s.i. Final pressure on tubing was 2225 p.s.i. Annulus of surface casing was monitored while the pressure test was underway, for any changes in the rate of bubbling. There were no abnormalities observed, indicating there is zonal isolation between the downhole injection zone, and the top-hole freshwater protection zones. The well has passed EPA's mechanical integrity test. PGE's remediation plan proposes the use of a resin material, with gas blocking capabilities. The resin will be pumped into the annular space of the surface casing at a depth of approximately 350', or the cap rock nearest this depth. This depth is determined to be below the deepest fresh groundwater in the area. It is anticipated that by placing the resin at this depth, the cap rock will be restored, thereby preventing the gas from permeating the micro-annulus that is allowing the gas to flow to surface. The resin has been used in similar annular gas scenarios, with success. An alternative procedure of pumping cement into the annular space has been discussed, but the outcome of this procedure is often times unpredictable, and could leave the casing integrity in a compromised condition. PGE anticipates that the resin will be available to them in April, of 2023. The product is currently in short supply, and the available stock has been allotted to other customers.

Comments: On April 7 2026, the Department conducted a complaint inspection of the H C McCullough 2 OG Well in regards to CTS 396257. Present during the inspection was Matt Woods (PADEP) and Darren Reilly (PADEP).The findings are as follows:At the time of the inspection the well appeared to be equipped for production. A wellhead was observed with a well tag fixed to it which contained the well name and API. No active fluid leaks or fluid discharges from the wellhead were observed at the surface. A production tank was observed onsite. Affixed to the production tank was a well posting which appeared to contain all required information in accordance with OGA3211(G) and OGA3211(H).Upon inspection of the production tank and associated piping, the Department observed what appeared to be a crack in the dump-line leading to the production tank. Under the apparent crack, the Department observed dark oil-like staining on the ground. The Department did not observe any fluid actively leaking from the cracked pipe at the time of the inspection. Conductivity readings of 0.07mS and 0.14mS were obtained in the area of dark staining. These readings appear comparable to the background conductivity reading of 0.16mS. While the conductivity readings do not suggest a brine release has occurred, it still appears a release (most likely hydrocarbon/oil based) is occurring/has occurred onsite.Prior to leaving the site, the Department contacted operator representative Heather Empfield via phone call. The Department informed Ms. Empfield of the observed crack in the piping as well as the staining on the ground directly beneath. Ms. Emfield stated field crews would assess the site and remediate any release as soon as possible.Based on today's inspection, violations are being issued for the observed release.

A wellhead was observed with a well tag fixed to it which contained the well name and API. No active fluid leaks or fluid discharges from the wellhead were observed at the surface. Comments: On 4/6/22 an incident inspection of the Pettit GH84 OG Well site was conducted in response to a report of spill received by the Department on 4/4/22. Initial details of the spill were reported by CNX at approximately 5:30pm on 4/4/22. The report stated that at approximately 3:30pm on 4/4/22 a leak was discovered around the valve of buried waterline at the GH84 well site. It was estimated that two barrels of brine were released. On 4/6/22 at approximately 8:45am, I called Kyle Borden of CNX to inquire about the spill. He stated that a leak was discovered in a buried three-inch polyline leading from the GH84 coalbed methane well to a tank battery. The leak was discovered by the lease operator during a routine inspection on 4/4/22. The well had previously been inspected on 3/30/22 and no leak was observed at that time. The lease operator observed an orange/red fluid saturating the ground behind the well pumpjack. The well was shut in upon discovery of the leak. Mr. Borden stated that excavation of the area began on 4/5/22. Due to overnight precipitation, the excavated area needed pumped the morning of 4/6/22. Mr. Borden stated that SPSI was contracted for remediation and Penn E&R was contracted for sampling. During the site inspection, the following was observed: -A crew was on-site excavating impacted substrate from the spill area (Photos #1-3 and #8). -No elevated conductivity was observed outside of the area that was actively being remediated. -BMPs were observed downslope of the disturbed area (Photos #5-6). -The area below the installed BMPs (Photo #7) did not exhibit elevated conductivity. -A well sign was posted at the pumpjack (Photo #9). Mr. Borden stated that after the initial remediation efforts, following the overnight precipitation, elevated conductivity was observed in the area that had been excavated. Upon further remediation of the area, Mr. Borden estimated that five barrels of brine were released. CNX plans to continue excavation of impacted material until elevated conductivity is no longer detected. An additional roll-off container was in route to the site at the time of the inspection. Mr. Borden stated that four roll-off boxes had already been filled and removed from the site. CNX is following Act 2 protocol for the spill. Violations of 78.57(a), SWMA 301, and 78.54 are being issued for the release.

Comments: On 9/01/2026, the DEP conducted a Compliance Schedule Evaluation (CSE) inspection at the Sproul well site in Stewart Township, Fayette County. This inspection also follows-up to IR 4211626, where the violation issued in IR 4206462 was left outstanding for failure to comply with the 5/01/2025 amendment of the 12/16/2021 COA.A Consent Order and Agreement (COA) was executed between the DEP and the operator on 12/16/2021. The First Modification to the COA was entered on 5/01/2025. The 12/16/2021 COA states that the operator "shall restore the Sproul 7005 Site in accordance with the restoration plan in the expired Sproul ESCGP, including but not limited to the installation of all Post Construction Stormwater Management Best Management Practices ("PCSM BMPs"). Restoration of the Sproul 7005 Well Site shall be completed by 10/30/2025." The operator shall then "submit a Notice of Termination ("NOT") for the Sproul ESCGP once permanent vegetation has been established at the Well Site in accordance with 25 Pa. Code 102.7. The NOT shall be submitted to the DEP no later than 12/31/2025. A Notice of Termination (NOT) request was submitted to the DEP by the operator on 12/31/2025.A notarized Post-Drilling Landowner Waiver of Well Site Restoration and the updated map requested in IR 4085078 were submitted with the operator's NOT request on 12/31/2025.However, the DEP observed possible soil cracking and soil displacement on the slope north of the well pad on 1/05/2026, at the time of IR 4119144. The operator reported on 1/16/2026, that they conducted repairs in this location and provided a photo of the repairs (IR 4128095). It appeared in the photo provided by the operator that the repair resulted in ground disturbances, as they applied temporary stabilization after completing their repairs. Therefore, the NOT request was denied on 1/30/2026 (IR 4133379).A violation was issued on 2/10/2026, for failure to comply with the 5/01/2025 amendment of the 12/16/2021 COA (IR 4140173).At the time of inspection, the following was observed:Mulch remains applied to the location where the potential soil cracking and soil displacement was identified in IR 4140173. However, since the time of IR 4211626, this location has exhibited 70% uniform and adequate vegetative growth coverage underneath the applied mulch, with no soil exposed (Photos 17-21). This location does not appear to threaten the Waters of the Commonwealth and/or well head integrity at the time of inspection. No evidence of further potential soil displacement was observed. The access road and well pad appear to be stable at the time of inspection with no observable accelerated erosion and sedimentation (Photos 4 and 22). No evidence of loose sediment flows was observed at the locations of the Sediment Trap and access road stormwater culvert (Photos 6-8 and 13-14). The previously sparse areas east of the well pad and on north side of soil stockpile are exhibiting 70% uniform and adequate vegetative growth coverage (Photos 5, 11, and 12).The gas well is equipped with a well tag and the operator's information (Photos 23 and 24). No evidence of a fluid leak was observed to the ground around the gas well. The Act 9 sign is installed at the entrance of the access road and is not obscured from view by vegetation, in accordance with 78a.55 (Photo 1). The Emergency Response Plan (ERP) and Preparedness Prevention and Contingency (PPC) plan are on site (Photos 2 and 3). The ERP and PPC plan appear to contain the sections required by 78a55.Based on today's inspection, the well site appears to have achieved permanent stabilization. The violation issued in IR 4140173 remains outstanding, as the expired ESCGP has not been terminated per the 12/16/2021 COA. Closure of the violation issued in IR 4140173 is contingent upon Department approval of an NOT request submitted by the Operator for this site.
